actions.action: Check leaf undersides and stems for fine webbing with a hand lens to rule out spider mites
Tap a stem over white paper or a sticky card to confirm thrips
Spot-test the alcohol spray on one leaf of a few plants and wait 48 hours
Dilute the alcohol spray further if browning appears
Spray plants with alcohol in the evening, out of direct sun
Remove badly damaged leaves and infested flowers, then bag and dispose of them outside the room
Hang blue sticky traps around the room to monitor thrips
Treat every 5-7 days for at least 4 weeks, rotating spinosad and insecticidal soap
For severe cases, apply a systemic such as imidacloprid per the label
Quarantine new or heavily infested plants

reason: The answer correctly identifies thrips, but it never mentions the beneficial predatory mites that actually solved the problem, relying instead on sprays and systemics; those are reasonable and not likely to harm the plant.
